name: Rust
description: A systems programming language focused on safety, speed and concurrency.
summary: In rust-lang/rust, cargo, clippy and other adopting repositories, LLMs may be used privately to answer questions, analyse, review and suggest, but not to create. LLM-written comments, issue bodies, PR descriptions and docs are banned; trivial changes, machine translation and verified LLM-found bugs need disclosure, and LLM-created code is only allowed in a pre-arranged, disclosed experiment.

evidence.quote: It’s fine to use LLMs to answer questions, analyze, distill, refine, check, suggest, review. But not to create.
Pre-arranged, non-critical, high-quality, well-tested, and well-reviewed code changes that are originally created by an LLM are allowed, with disclosure.
Your contributions are your responsibility; you cannot place any blame on an LLM.
Using an LLM to discover bugs, as long as you personally verify the bug.
This also applies to issue bodies and PR descriptions.
Comments that are originally created by an LLM posted from a personal user account.
All uses under “⚠️ Allowed with caveats” must disclose that an LLM was used.
